answer: Submissions that land within 81 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The lagoon detector writes to ivory, and horizon reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 24 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 21 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
